case.summary: Verdict: fraud at probability 0.77 for the card_not_present_new_device pattern. The episode is the single flagged online purchase, transaction 3534820 for $59.67 on card C09988-K1, made on a device profile ("Windows | NULL | edge 16.0 | NULL") never before seen on this card, so exposure is $59.67. Decisive evidence: the customer family (C09988 denies the charge; in this bank's history 4,665/4,665 such denials were confirmed fraud) corroborated by the memory family (the case-memory scorer rates the transaction 0.45/calibrated 0.53, and six to eight closed cases — CC-3491, CC-5057, CC-2694, CC-2898, CC-2540, CC-3580 — with the same device-profile overlap were all confirmed fraud with this exact pattern); no legitimacy family emerged (the amount fell inside the card's baseline, but that alone doesn't offset the denial). We asked for step-up authentication before finalizing a block; the simulated reply was inconclusive/no response within the window, so per R4 we assume non-completion rather than a pass. An alternative reading is possible if the customer's device change reflects a genuine new-phone purchase with no supporting evidence of compromise, but the denial plus the strong same-device fraud precedent outweigh that. The bank should now, via the L1 approval route, block card C09988-K1, decline any pending authorization on it, and keep it on monitoring while the case stays open; escalation and SAR filing are not triggered since exposure is well under $500/$1,000 and no shared-origin cluster was found.
